According to standard testing methods, what is the maximum allowable expansion of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) in the Le Chatelier test?
e: The Le Chatelier test measures cement soundness due to uncombined lime. IS codes strictly mandate that the maximum expansion for OPC must not exceed 10 mm to prevent structural cracking.

q: What is the generally accepted maximum limit of water absorption for a good quality building stone?
e: A good building stone should be dense and non-porous. Standard engineering specifications state that it should reject water, with absorption not exceeding 5% of its dry weight after 24 hours of immersion.

q: In standard plywood manufacturing, the number of individual wood veneers used is always:
e: Plywood is always manufactured with an odd number of layers (e.g., 3, 5, 7). This maintains symmetry around the central core layer, which physically prevents the board from warping or twisting under moisture changes.

q: According to IS 1077, what is the minimum required compressive strength for a "Second-Class" burnt clay brick?
e: First-class bricks must have a minimum crushing strength of 10.5 N/mm² (105 kg/cm²), while second-class bricks must meet a minimum threshold of 7.0 N/mm² (70 kg/cm²).

q: Which common substance acts as a powerful chemical "retarder" when added to a cement concrete mix?
e: Sugar is a highly effective, low-cost retarder. Even a small fraction of a percent of sugar added to a concrete mix will significantly delay the initial setting time of the cement paste.

q: What is the standard size of the concrete cube specimen used in laboratories to test the 28-day compressive strength of concrete?
e: Standard IS codes (IS 516) universally mandate a mold size of 150 mm × 150 mm × 150 mm for testing the compressive strength of normal structural concrete.

q: In brick masonry, which specific bond features alternate headers and stretchers laid within the exact same course?
e: The Flemish bond is defined by alternating headers and stretchers in every single row. It provides an aesthetically pleasing appearance but is slightly weaker than the English bond.

q: According to the Mandatory Rules of Thumb (NBC 205) for RCC framed structures, what is the minimum required diameter for longitudinal reinforcing bars in a column?
e: The Nepal National Building Code strictly specifies that vertical (longitudinal) steel bars used in load-bearing RCC columns must be at least 12 mm in diameter to safely handle buckling and seismic forces.

q: In scaffolding structures, what is the specific technical name for the horizontal tubes that directly support the wooden working platform?
e: Putlogs are the transverse horizontal members. One end rests on the ledger (or inside the wall), and they directly carry the wooden planks that workers stand on.

q: In project management, what specific chart is most commonly used to visually schedule and track the duration of various construction activities?
e: A Gantt chart is a standard bar chart used universally in construction scheduling. It clearly displays the start dates, durations, and overlapping sequences of all site activities.

q: In a municipal water distribution main, which specific valve is used to manually regulate or completely stop the flow of water for maintenance?
e: A sluice valve (also known as a gate valve) is installed along the main pipeline to isolate sections of the network, allowing operators to shut off the water supply during repairs.

q: In sanitary plumbing, what is the standard recommended depth of the "water seal" inside a domestic trap to effectively block sewer gases?
e: Sanitary engineering textbooks specify a water seal depth between 25 mm and 75 mm (typically around 50 mm). This is deep enough to resist evaporation and back-pressure, but shallow enough to flush cleanly.

q: In modern single-phase electrical wiring systems, which insulation color is strictly standardized for the "Phase" (Live) wire?
e: Standard electrical safety protocols mandate Red (in older South Asian codes) or Brown (in updated international codes) to clearly identify the dangerous, current-carrying live phase wire.

q: In artificial lighting design, what is the standard SI unit used to measure the intensity of illumination arriving on a specific surface (like a desk)?
e: Lux is the measurement of illuminance. It strictly defines how much luminous flux (Lumens) successfully reaches and spreads across a one-square-meter area of a given surface.
